methodological_rigor.justification: The PROMETEO trial is a well-designed single-arm phase II window-of-opportunity study with pre-specified primary endpoint (RCB-0/I rate), registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT03802604), with protocol and SAP available in supplementary. Multiple serial biopsies at 5 timepoints provide comprehensive biomarker data. Statistical testing for TIL/immune biomarker changes used appropriate paired analyses with FDR correction for gene expression. However, the single-arm design prevents attribution of efficacy to T-VEC vs. atezolizumab alone; only 28 patients enrolled over 3 years at 4 sites limits statistical power for secondary biomarker-response correlations; DFS analysis is post-hoc; and the comparison to historical rates is not pre-specified.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a single-arm phase II trial (LoE 4) addressing the important clinical problem of residual disease after NAC in HER2-negative breast cancer. The 26.9% RCB-0/I rate including 30% pCR in HR+/HER2- (an immunologically cold subtype) is notably promising. The window-of-opportunity design provides both efficacy data and rich translational biology. No control arm prevents definitive efficacy assessment. The 4-year DFS of 100% in pCR patients at 44.6 months median follow-up is encouraging but based on very small numbers (n=7).

reporting_quality.justification: The trial is registered (NCT03802604), CONSORT diagram provided (Extended Data Fig. 1), protocol and SAP available in supplementary information, and central pathology review with blinding is described. Adverse events are reported per CTCAE v4.03 with grade stratification. RNAseq raw data is deposited in EGA (EGAS50000001499), providing good data availability. Minor deficiencies include reporting on TILs from some patients without invasive tumor cells and the post-hoc nature of DFS analysis which is not explicitly distinguished from pre-specified secondary endpoints.

novelty_literature.justification: The PROMETEO trial is among the first studies to evaluate T-VEC combined with anti-PD-L1 in the preoperative window after NAC for HER2-negative breast cancer including the HR+/HER2- subtype. The sequential T-VEC priming followed by atezolizumab combination strategy is a meaningful clinical extension of prior T-VEC + ICI work (MASTERKEY-265). The observation of pCR in 30% of HR+/HER2- patients and the detailed longitudinal immune profiling data provide novel translational insights. The approach is incremental rather than paradigm-shifting.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-written and well-organized, with a clear study design schematic, comprehensive patient tables, and detailed biomarker sections. The discussion thoughtfully contextualizes results within prior literature on T-VEC, atezolizumab, and the HR+/HER2- immunotherapy landscape. Limitations are explicitly and thoroughly acknowledged. Minor issues include some figure elements that appear abbreviated and the somewhat confusing relationship between RCB assessment and the null hypothesis rejection claim.

key_strengths: Pre-specified primary endpoint (RCB-0/I) met with statistical significance; 30% pCR in HR+/HER2- breast cancer is notably high in this immunologically cold subtype
Comprehensive serial biopsy design with 5 timepoints, centralized pathology, TIL assessment, PAM50 subtyping, and RNAseq providing rich translational dataset
RNAseq raw data deposited in EGA (EGAS50000001499) and full protocol/SAP available, demonstrating excellent data transparency
100% 4-year DFS in pCR patients at median 44.6 months follow-up supports prognostic significance of the primary endpoint
Favorable safety profile with no grade 4-5 AEs supporting feasibility of combination in pre-surgical window
key_concerns: Single-arm design without atezolizumab-alone or T-VEC-alone control arm prevents attribution of efficacy to specific treatment components
Small sample size (n=28, only 8 TNBC) severely limits subgroup analyses and biomarker-response correlations
DFS analysis and survival outcomes are post-hoc with very small event numbers (n=4 events) limiting conclusions
Trial used atezolizumab which has not shown benefit in NAC-based TNBC trials; current standard includes pembrolizumab, limiting contemporary comparability
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a well-conducted phase II window-of-opportunity trial with strong translational endpoints, data transparency, and encouraging efficacy signals in HER2-negative breast cancer; limitations inherent to the single-arm design and small cohort are acknowledged and appropriate for this developmental stage, supporting acceptance with minor revisions at a tier-2 journal.
